text:
jia: heads up — profiler shows a p95 latency bump for streamed responses when continuous-batching is enabled and seq lengths drift around ~600 tokens. see kernel-selection churn + KV miss spike.

ben: ok. is this only on the new kernel fallback path or across the board?

jia: mainly when selector flips between small-k and wide-k kernels mid-request. stack shows repeated kernel load/unload and KV entries getting evicted. logs: "kv: evict id=0x7f3a" repeated.

sam: can you share the trace?

jia: trace: https://perf.example/org/trace/abcd — look at the region ~t=3.2s, you can see partial-decode restarts.

maria: rough thought: reduce sensitivity of kernel re-eval by adding a smoothing window on observed sequence length and require a margin before switching. also consider a short stream-flush hold to coalesce tokens instead of partial-decoding every few ms. :thinking_face:

ben: +1. switching too eagerly is creating tail work. even 30–50ms of coalescing could avoid a decode restart.

sam: tradeoff is head-of-line latency for small responses — need safe guard so tiny single-token responses don't wait.

maria: propose heuristic: if pending_stream_tokens < 32 and expected_seq_growth > 64 then hold up to 50ms; otherwise flush immediately. and only re-eval kernel if running_avg_len changes by >15%.

jia: config sketch:
```
kernel_reval_margin: 0.15
token_budget_smoothing: 12s
stream_flush_hold_ms: 50
pending_token_threshold: 32
```

jia: i'll run three experiments on canary: A) smoothing window=12s, B) flush_hold=50ms, C) conservative kernel re-eval (15% margin). will measure p50/p95 and KV miss-rate.

perf-bot: quick snapshot from previous run: p95=118ms, KV miss-rate=3.6% 

deploy-bot: canary scheduled on pool-rt-4 at 05:30 UTC — rolling 10% traffic.

ben: please add unit tests for selector stability and an integration test that simulates streaming + KV churn. also capture perf counters for kernel load/unload events.

jia: adding tests now, sending draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt/pull/789 — will post results here after canary.

sam: if we still see regressions, fallback plan: snapshot KV state before kernel switch and warm it after switch instead of letting misses hit the model. could be slightly slower but avoids repeated decode restarts.

maria: agreed. good path. :rocket:

jia: thx — will report back with canary metrics (latency, KV miss-rate, kernel switch count).
